mission: US-legal-venue sweep for the mechanical-lock shape (outcome confirmable from a free public feed before the venue reprices), per venue_expansion/GROUNDING.md
headline_finding: ForecastEx (IBKR's CFTC-regulated Forecast Contract exchange) lists daily high/low-temperature threshold-ladder contracts on Weather Underground station data for 27+ cities (20 US + 7 international as of 2026-07-22), with genuinely large live volume (e.g. UHLAX 651,446 pairs, UHSFO 153,414 pairs, UHLGA 95,992 pairs on 2026-07-22 alone) and a free, unauthenticated, per-trade-timestamped public data lake (forecastex-public-data S3 bucket) updated intraday. This is a structurally new, US-legal, real candidate for the mechanical-lock shape that this repo has not previously studied. It was found and verified with live requests, not just secondary reporting. CAVEAT: ForecastEx's transaction fee is a FLAT $0.01/contract per side, independent of price -- unlike Kalshi's quadratic fee or Polymarket's 0.05*p*(1-p) fee, this does NOT shrink near p->1, so it eats a much larger fraction of the thin 1-2c gap the mechanical-lock edge targets. Needs a dedicated fee-inclusive EV study before any GO call -- not run here, this is a discovery/access sweep only.
second_finding: Polymarket US (QCX LLC, the CFTC-regulated, US-person-legal product referenced in ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md §6) is CONFIRMED NOT to currently list the daily temperature bracket-ladder product studied on the global (geo-blocked) venue. As of this scan it is sports-first (launched Dec 2025 / relaunched May 2026), with politics/weather described in secondary press as 'coming' or 'dabbling' but not verifiable as live in the app-store listing or the exchange's own developer page, which lists no weather/temperature category. Its API additionally requires an application + approval process (sandbox, then production credentials) -- not open/public like the global venue's Gamma/CLOB APIs. This resolves the single most valuable open question in §6 of the prior verdict: NO, not yet, as of 2026-07-23.

venues.name: ForecastEx (IBKR ForecastTrader)
venues.operator: ForecastEx LLC, wholly owned subsidiary of Interactive Brokers Group
venues.regulatory_status: CFTC-registered Designated Contract Market (DCM) + Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO). Began operations 2024-08-01. US-legal, no geo-block for US persons -- this is IBKR's own regulated product.
venues.products_of_interest_detail: ‘Daily Temperature Forecast Contract’ (product code U[H/L/A][3-letter station code], filed with CFTC 2026-01-23 under Reg 40.2(a); PDF verified: https://forecastex-public-data.s3.amazonaws.com/product_filings/Daily%20Temperature%20Forecast%20Contract.pdf). Event question: 'Will the [highest/lowest/average] temperature in [region] [exceed/be below] [##] F on [date]?' -- ForecastEx lists ~9 consecutive integer strikes per city-day, which collectively form the same threshold-ladder shape as Kalshi's KXHIGH*/Polymarket's bracket ladders. Live 2026-07-22 volume pulled directly from the venue's own daily_summary CSV (see evidence): UHLAX (LA) 651,446 pairs, UHSFO (SF) 153,414, UHLGA (NYC) 95,992, UHSEA (Seattle) 33,778, UHPHX (Phoenix) 20,591, plus UHATL/UHAUS/UHBKF(Denver)/UHBNA/UHBOS/UHCLT/UHDCA/UHDFW/UHDTW/UHHOU/UHJAX/UHMDW(Chicago)/UHMIA/UHMSP/UHOKC/UHPHL/UHSAT and ~20 corresponding low-temp (ULxxx) tickers, all with nonzero same-day volume. International: SHDDF (Frankfurt), SHFPO (Paris), SHJTT (Tokyo), SHSSS (Singapore), SHSSY (Sydney), SHYHC (Vancouver), SHYYZ (Toronto) -- smaller volume (40-740 pairs) but live. Also separately: Monthly/Annual global-temperature-threshold contracts, HDD/CDD-style 'Temperature Degree Days Forecast Contract', hurricane landfall/category/count families, precipitation totals, severe weather -- not the daily-lock shape, not examined further here.
venues.settlement_source: Weather Underground (wunderground.com) station-history display -- the SAME third-party scrape source Polymarket's global venue uses for its NYC temperature ladder (per ref/wx_new_capacity_scan.md), so any basis-risk finding from a future Polymarket study likely transfers. Resolution Time = 'the time at which the first temperature observation for any subsequent calendar day is published by Weather Underground for the applicable station' -- i.e. formal settlement is always next-day, contract text explicitly states 'This contract is not subject to early Resolution.' This does NOT preclude the mechanical-lock TRADE (buying before the book reprices once the day's extreme looks decided intraday) -- it only means ForecastEx itself won't settle the contract early even if the outcome looks locked; the tradable inefficiency, if any, would be in the book's slowness to reprice to the locked value before formal EOD settlement, same structural shape as Kalshi/Polymarket.
venues.public_market_data_access_detail: Free, fully public, UNAUTHENTICATED S3-backed data lake at https://forecastex-public-data.s3.amazonaws.com (browsable at https://data.forecastex.com/), verified live via direct curl/S3 REST calls (no API key, no login). Three CSV families, one file per calendar day, back to 2024-08-01: (1) pairs/pairs_YYYYMMDD.csv -- every matched trade with per-contract yes/no price, quantity, and a MILLISECOND pair_time timestamp (verified: today's file, pairs_20260723.csv, already contained trades timestamped up to 16:14:59 CT as of this scan, i.e. updates intraday, not just end-of-day); (2) prices/daily_prices_YYYYMMDD.csv -- daily OHLC + settlement + VWAP per contract/subtype; (3) daily_summary/summary_YYYYMMDD.csv -- per-product total_pairs (volume) rollup. This is finer-grained (individual timestamped fills) than what either Kalshi's public trade history or Polymarket's prices-history endpoint offers for free, and is a strong candidate feed for the fill-quality / EV backtest that the mechanical-lock strategy needs. For LIVE order-book depth and order placement, access is via IBKR's TWS/Client Portal Web API (Event Contracts in the Web API, per IBKR Campus docs) -- this requires an ordinary IBKR brokerage account (the standard, non-exotic path to trade ForecastEx contracts at all), not a separate application/approval gate the way Polymarket US's institutional API is gated.
venues.fees: $0.01 per contract, charged to BOTH the Yes and No side at execution, independent of price/resolution/netting/settlement (verified from primary source: https://forecastex-public-data.s3.amazonaws.com/regulatory/ForecastEx_Fee_Schedule.pdf). Structural note: this is a FLAT fee that does not shrink as price approaches $1, unlike Kalshi's ceil(7*p*(1-p))/100 or Polymarket's 0.05*p*(1-p) which both -> 0 near the locked extreme. At a hypothetical ask=0.98 lock-capture entry, ForecastEx's $0.01 fee consumes half the theoretical 2c gross edge -- materially worse fee economics for THIS SPECIFIC strategy shape than either prior venue, even though the product and feed otherwise look promising. Contracts also carry a monthly 'incentive coupon' on collateral (per Rule 612(c)) -- a yield feature, not relevant to the per-trade edge calc.
venues.mechanical_lock_shape_caveat: Structurally present (threshold ladder + free public near-real-time feed + third-party settlement source with same basis-risk profile as Polymarket's known-thin coverage problem + flat fee that specifically hurts this strategy). NOT validated -- no backtest, no false-lock rate, no book-repricing-speed measurement done in this scan. This is a discovery finding only; a dedicated study (structurally identical to pmkt_gap_study.py / pmkt_final_verdict.py, swapping in ForecastEx's data lake) is the clear next step.
evidence: https://forecastex-public-data.s3.amazonaws.com/product_filings/Daily%20Temperature%20Forecast%20Contract.pdf (fetched and read in full, cached at venue_expansion/cache/fx_daily_temp.pdf)
https://forecastex-public-data.s3.amazonaws.com/regulatory/ForecastEx_Fee_Schedule.pdf (fetched and read in full, cached at venue_expansion/cache/forecastex/fee_schedule.pdf)

venues.name: CME Group (event/weather contracts)
venues.regulatory_status: CFTC-registered DCM (CME itself), the incumbent institutional derivatives exchange. Weather products are exchange-listed futures/options, not retail 'event contracts.'
venues.products_of_interest_detail: Lists HDD (Heating Degree Day), CDD (Cooling Degree Day), and CAT (Cumulative Average Temperature) contracts across 18 cities (13 US, 4 Europe, 1 Asia -- includes Chicago, NYC, London, Amsterdam, Tokyo, and newer additions Paris/Essen/Burbank/Houston/Philadelphia/Boston). These are MONTHLY/SEASONAL index-average products, not daily-high/low brackets: settlement is an accumulated or averaged index over the full month/season, so there is no single intraday 'mechanical lock' moment analogous to a daily-max threshold being cleared -- the whole point of the mechanical-lock edge (a same-day observable extreme that locks a same-day settlement before the book catches up) does not have a matching daily-granularity CME product. Same structural failure mode as the already-killed Rain Sleeve / monthly-accumulator family in ref/GROUNDING.md's graveyard.
venues.public_market_data_access: Institutional-grade only: traded via CME Direct or Trayport, accessed through CME Globex/ClearPort, requires a futures broker relationship -- not a self-serve retail app or an open public API/feed. Free public pages (cmegroup.com) give marketing-level descriptions only, not tradable data.
venues.fees: Not determined -- gated behind broker relationships, exchange + clearing fee schedules not retail-published in an easily comparable per-contract-cent form the way Kalshi/Polymarket/ForecastEx are.

recommended_next_step: ForecastEx's Daily Temperature Forecast Contract is the one finding in this sweep that clears the bar for a real study, structurally analogous to how Polymarket cleared the bar in ref/wx_new_capacity_scan.md Q1: (1) measure false-lock rate against Weather Underground's specific station pages (same basis-risk question already flagged unmeasured for Polymarket -- may share the same answer since it's the same data source); (2) measure book-repricing speed intraday using the pairs_*.csv per-trade timestamps (already confirmed to exist at millisecond granularity, free, back to 2024-08-01); (3) run the fee-inclusive EV calc with ForecastEx's flat $0.01/contract fee explicitly, since this fee shape (unlike Kalshi/Polymarket) does NOT favor near-certainty entries -- this could kill the venue on fee economics alone even if the lock signal itself is clean, and should be checked FIRST since it's a two-line calculation, before any further data pulls. Do not build a Polymarket US study until the company confirms a live weather category (recheck periodically -- cheap).
